html:
At Rumbula forest near Riga, on two days in late 1941, German forces and Latvian collaborators shot about 25,000 Jews from the Riga ghetto. It was one of the largest mass killings of the Holocaust before the death camps.

Germany had taken Latvia in July 1941. The SS commander Friedrich Jeckeln, who had organised the massacre at Babi Yar in Ukraine, planned it. The victims were marched from the ghetto to pits in the forest. Members of the Latvian Arājs Kommando took part.

The ghetto was then filled with Jews deported from Germany. Of about 70,000 Jews in Latvia in 1941, very few survived. Jeckeln was tried and hanged in Riga in 1946. Compare the Ponary massacre in Lithuania.
sum: At Rumbula forest near Riga, on two days in late 1941, German forces and Latvian collaborators shot about 25,000 Jews from the Riga ghetto. It was one of the largest mass killings of the Holocaust before the death camps.
